title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
content_md: Cybersecurity firm FoxIO has disclosed three vulnerabilities in GoAhead’s handling of TLS. They could keep revoked client certificates working, let eavesdroppers decrypt some traffic, or help attackers get around a cap on certificate chain length. GoAhead, a lightweight web server made by EmbedThis, runs the management interfaces of networking equipment, printers and industrial systems. According to FoxIO, it is present on hundreds of millions of devices across the IoT, OT, firewall and military sectors. FoxIO’s Sébastien Féry, who documented the flaws this week , said each one affects only a subset of deployments. Which GoAhead devices are at risk depends on the TLS library the manufacturer built into the firmware and how it configured certificate checks. The critical flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS score of 9.1), impacts GoAhead 3.4.5 through 6.1.0 when built with OpenSSL or a compatible library and configured for mutual TLS (mTLS) with a certificate revocation list (CRL). The server reads the list but never tells OpenSSL to consult it. On these builds, a certificate an administrator has revoked, such as one tied to a stolen or compromised device, is still accepted, even with issuer verification switched on. Nothing at startup warns that revocation checks are inactive. The eavesdropping risk comes from the second bug (CVSS score of 5.9, no CVE), found in GoAhead 4.0.2 through 6.1.0 builds that use Mbed TLS.
